title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

reading.body:
This is a case of an automated alert being treated as a positive identification. License plate cameras flagged a stolen Camaro linked to aggravated robberies, and that flag was enough to bring at least five patrol cars and a helicopter down on a different Camaro. The stop proceeded to guns drawn and handcuffs before anyone confirmed the vehicle was the one being sought.

The failure sits at the handoff between the alert and the stop, the point where a database hit becomes an armed encounter. Deputies and the helicopter could not read the plates on the car they stopped, so the one check that would have separated the two vehicles was unavailable at the moment it mattered. Catching this would have required a confirmed plate read, or a rule that an unverified alert cannot escalate to a felony stop, before the decision to surround the car was made.

What is not established is what specifically prompted deputies to stop this particular Camaro, since the summary does not say. The threat to shoot and kill is Julian's account, not a finding. The men were not charged, the sheriff's office review is a review and not a conclusion, and Leslie's plan to hire an attorney is a stated intention rather than an outcome.

reports.title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

summary:
On Aug. 3 in Cypress, Texas, Harris County sheriff's deputies mistook two 19 year old men, Anthony and Julian, for car thieves. Deputies surrounded Anthony's Camaro, with at least five patrol cars arriving and a helicopter circling, then pointed guns and handcuffed them. Julian said a deputy pushed him to the ground and threatened to shoot and kill him. Deputies soon realized it was the wrong car. The stolen Camaro had been flagged by license plate cameras and linked to aggravated robberies, but deputies and the helicopter could not read the plates on the car they stopped.

The men were not charged. Anthony's mother, Leslie, said she plans to hire an attorney and wants deputies held accountable. The Harris County Sheriff's Office said supervisors, including the district captain, shift lieutenants, and shift sergeants, will review body camera video to check whether procedures were followed. The men were given information on filing a formal complaint with internal affairs, and both plan to do so.
title_en: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say
